title: Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) – Ethical Framework
html:
1. Purpose

To establish an ethical management framework ensuring all hospital operations, clinical practices, and management decisions are conducted with integrity, transparency, accountability, and fairness in accordance with NABH standards.

2. Scope

This SOP applies to all:

  • Hospital leadership and governing body members
  • Clinical, administrative, technical, and support staff
  • Volunteers, trainees affiliated with the hospital

3. References

  • NABH 6th Edition, Chapter: Responsibility of Management (ROM)
  • NABH 6th Edition, Chapter: Patient Rights and Education (PRE)
  • Hospital Code of Conduct and Ethics Policy
  • National and State laws on medical ethics and professional conduct
  • Medical Council of India (MCI)/National Medical Commission (NMC) Code of Ethics

4. Definitions

TermDefinition
Ethical FrameworkA structured system defining the hospital’s ethical values, policies, and procedures for handling ethical issues.
Ethics CommitteeA multidisciplinary committee established to review and resolve ethical dilemmas and guide staff.
Conflict of Interest (COI)A situation where a person’s private interests could improperly influence professional duties or decisions.
Ethical DilemmaA situation involving competing moral principles where the correct course of action is unclear.

5. Responsibility

RoleResponsibility
CEO / Medical DirectorEnsure implementation and periodic review of the ethical framework.
Ethics CommitteeOversee ethical policies, review cases, and recommend corrective actions.
Quality ManagerEnsure integration of ethical practices in hospital quality systems and audits.
Department HeadsPromote adherence to ethics and escalate ethical concerns.
All EmployeesFollow ethical conduct, report violations, and uphold patient rights.

6. Policy Statement

  • The hospital shall maintain the highest ethical standards in patient care, research, and management.
  • All employees shall comply with laws, regulations, and NABH standards.
  • The hospital shall provide mechanisms for reporting unethical behaviour confidentially.
  • Decisions shall be free from conflict of interest, discrimination, or undue influence.
  • The hospital shall operate with transparency, sustainability, and social responsibility.

7. Procedure

7.1 Establishing the Ethical Framework

  • The Ethics Committee (EC) is constituted by the management.
  • The EC includes representatives from:
    • Medical staff
    • Nursing
    • Administration
    • HR / Legal
    • Quality Department
    • External member
  • The EC meets quarterly or as needed to review ethical issues.

7.2 Ethical Code of Conduct

  • Every employee shall sign a Code of Conduct upon joining.
  • The Code shall include:
    • Patient care ethics (respect, autonomy, confidentiality)
    • Staff behaviour (honesty, respect, professionalism)
    • Financial integrity (no kickbacks, fair billing)
    • Environmental and social responsibilities
  • Any violation of the Code will trigger disciplinary procedures.

7.3 Managing Ethical Dilemmas

  • Ethical concerns can be reported by:
    • Staff → Supervisor / Ethics Committee / HR
    • Patients → Complaint/Grievance Desk
  • Complaints can be submitted via:
    • Written form (Ethical Concern Form)
    • Anonymous drop box or email
  • The Ethics Committee:
    • Reviews and classifies the case (minor/major)
    • Conducts investigation or mediation
    • Recommends corrective or preventive action (CAPA)
  • Documentation is maintained confidentially by the Quality Department.

7.4 Conflict of Interest (COI) Declaration

  • All leadership and staff must annually submit a Conflict of Interest Declaration Form.
  • Any potential COI must be disclosed before engaging in:
    • Procurement decisions
    • Clinical trials / research
    • Vendor relationships
    • Employment of relatives
  • Undeclared COI will result in disciplinary action.

7.5 Transparency and Ownership Disclosure

  • The hospital shall display:
    • Ownership details
    • Affiliations and accreditations
    • Clinical outcomes (quality indicators)
  • All advertisements and publications must reflect truthful and verifiable information.

7.6 Sustainability & Social Responsibility

  • The hospital will:
    • Implement waste segregation and energy conservation measures.
    • Conduct community outreach programs (e.g., health camps, awareness drives).
    • Maintain an annual report on sustainability initiatives.
  • The management reviews environmental and social metrics annually.

7.7 Training and Communication

  • All employees shall receive ethics training:
    • During induction
    • Annually (refresher training)
  • Ethics case discussions will be included in clinical meetings.
  • Posters and intranet messages shall promote hospital ethical values.

7.8 Monitoring and Review

  • The Quality Department will track:
    • Number of ethical issues raised and resolved
    • Staff trained on ethics (%)
    • COI declarations submitted (%)
    • Sustainability targets achieved
  • The Ethics Committee will submit a quarterly report to management.
  • The Ethical Framework SOP will be reviewed annually or when NABH standards are updated.
